name: Mepazine

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market in United States, first in 1970 — for blood vessel problems, stomach and gut problems and nerve and brain harm

similar.name: Thioridazine

summary: Mepazine was pulled from the United States market starting in 1970 due to damage to blood vessels, digestive system harm, and damage to the nervous system [3]. In tests done by a small computer model rather than on people, the drug received a medium risk score for liver harm and a high risk score for heart harm [M]. Other medications that are chemically similar to Mepazine have been pulled from markets or given strong boxed warnings for liver, heart, psychiatric, or infectious disease problems [3][4][5].
